mainTopic: Placing לשכת הטלאים in the southwest, the right-turn rule, and the כהן גדול's first choice of offerings and portions, including אביי's answer about the שתי הלחם
overview: This amud finishes the discussion about the chambers of the בית המקדש. The גמרא proves that לשכת הטלאים was in the southwest corner, because only then does רב הונא's answer about לחם הפנים work. It then asks how a תנא could list the chambers moving to the left, when every turn must be to the right. The answer is that the right-turn rule applies only during actual עבודה, and here the תנא is only counting the chambers. Next the גמרא quotes the משנה: the כהן גדול offers first and takes his portion first. A ברייתא explains that he simply announces which offering he will bring or eat, and that he takes one of the שתי הלחם and four or five of the לחם הפנים. רבי says he always takes five, half for אהרן and half for his sons. The גמרא asks why the ברייתא seems to switch between רבי and רבנן. אביי answers that the first clauses follow רבנן: the כהן גדול gets a whole loaf of the שתי הלחם only because a broken piece is not respectful for him.

steps.title: Proof from the answer about the showbread
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא's answer about the two משניות on לחם הפנים only works if לשכת הטלאים was in the southwest.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say the Chamber of the Lambs was in the southwest. That is how רב הונא settles the contradiction about לחם הפנים. But if you say it was in the northwest, then in the end, what answer is there about לחם הפנים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to prove where לשכת הטלאים stood. It points out that רב הונא's answer to the contradiction about לחם הפנים only works under one of the two options.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא explained that the two משניות list the chambers in different directions: one goes to the right and one goes to the left. If לשכת הטלאים was in the southwest, this explains what both משניות say about the chamber where לחם הפנים was made. If it was in the northwest, then whichever direction you go, another chamber (לשכת החותמות) stands in between, so the contradiction about לחם הפנים is still there.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense if you say… (opens a proof: this option works, the other does not)
The showbread, twelve loaves placed on the שולחן each שבת

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
that it (the Chamber of the Lambs) was in the southwest,
that is how he (Rav Huna) resolves
the showbread against the showbread (one mishnah against the other).
phrases.notes: Two משניות seem to contradict each other about which chamber sits next to the chamber of the לחם הפנים.

phrases.english: But if you say
it was in the northwest,
in the end, what is the resolution
of the showbread?!
phrases.notes: לשכת החותמות would stand in between, so the contradiction would remain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (on the previous amud) about where לשכת הטלאים was located.
steps.raayaObject: That לשכת הטלאים was in the southwest corner.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's resolution of the contradiction between the mishnayos about לחם הפנים.

steps.title: Conclusion: the Chamber of the Lambs was in the southwest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the proof that לשכת הטלאים was in the southwest.
steps.simpleTranslation: So must we not learn from this that it was in the southwest? Yes, learn it from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion of the proof and accepts it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since only the southwest location lets רב הונא's answer work, the גמרא settles on that location. The phrase שמע מינה said a second time means the proof is fully accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that…
Learn from this; when repeated, it means the conclusion is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: לשכת הטלאים was in the southwest corner. This is proven because רב הונא's answer about לחם הפנים needs it.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from this
that it was in the southwest?
Learn from it (indeed, so it is).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of the proof in Step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: לשכת הטלאים was in the southwest corner.

steps.title: Challenge: every turn must be to the right
steps.stepSummary: How can one תנא list the chambers going to the left, when every turn in the מקדש must be to the right?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the Master say: all turns that you make should only be to the right, toward the east?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's idea that one תנא lists the chambers going to the left. It quotes a rule that every turn in the מקדש must be to the right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's answer depends on one משנה moving to the left. A well-known rule says that כהנים always turn to the right. So how could a תנא describe a leftward path?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't the Master say… (introduces a challenge from a known teaching)
By way of the right, turning to the right

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
all turns that you turn
should be only
by way of the right, toward the east?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the leftward-counting idea that the proof in Step 1 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that one תנא lists the chambers moving to the left.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a fixed rule that all turns in the מקדש are to the right, so a leftward route seems impossible.

steps.title: Answer: the right-turn rule is only for actual service
steps.stepSummary: Turning right is required only during עבודה. Here the תנא is just counting the chambers.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only to the Temple service. But here it is just a counting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The rule of turning right applies only when a כהן is actually doing עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No כהן actually walked from chamber to chamber in this order. The תנא is only listing them. So a list can go in either direction without breaking the right-turn rule.

keyTerms.meaning: These words (this rule) apply only to…

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not cancel the right-turn rule. It only limits the rule to actual עבודה, not to describing where things are.

phrases.english: These words apply to the service.
But here —
it is merely a counting.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The right-turn rule applies to any description of movement in the מקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The right-turn rule applies only to actual עבודה, not to listing the chambers.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the High Priest goes first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that the כהן גדול offers and takes his portion first.
steps.simpleTranslation: [As the משנה said:] The כהן גדול offers a portion first and takes a portion first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This line sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the כהן גדול two special rights. He may choose which offering to bring, and he may choose which portion to eat, without waiting for the lottery or the normal sharing. The next steps explain how this works.

keyTerms.meaning: Offers a portion first (he picks before others)

phrases.english: As the High Priest offers a portion first
and takes a portion first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול has first choice both in offering and in taking portions.

steps.title: How the High Priest offers first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the כהן גדול simply announces which offering he will bring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: How does he offer a portion first? He says, 'This עולה I am offering,' or 'This מנחה I am offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא explains the first right. The כהן גדול just says out loud which offering he wants to bring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary כהנים are assigned tasks by a lottery. The כהן גדול skips the lottery. His spoken choice is enough to claim the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt-offering, burned completely on the מזבח

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
How does he offer a portion first?
He says: 'This burnt-offering I am offering,'
'This meal-offering I am offering.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כֵּיצַד מַקְרִיב חֵלֶק בָּרֹאשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of the משנה quoted in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול claims an offering simply by announcing it.

steps.title: How the High Priest takes his portion first
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול announces which חטאת or אשם he will eat. He also takes one of the שתי הלחם loaves and four or five of the לחם הפנים loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he take a portion first? He says, 'This חטאת I am eating,' or 'This אשם I am eating.' He also takes one loaf of the two loaves, and four or five of the showbread.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the second right. The כהן גדול chooses which offerings he will eat, and he gets a larger share of the special breads.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With חטאת and אשם, he simply announces which one he will eat. From the שתי הלחם of שבועות he takes one of the two loaves. From the לחם הפנים he takes four or five, and the next step argues over this number.

keyTerms.meaning: The two loaves (שתי הלחם) brought on שבועות

phrases.english: How does he take a portion first?
He says: 'This sin-offering I am eating,'
'This guilt-offering I am eating.'
And he takes one loaf of the two loaves,
four or five
of the showbread loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of the משנה quoted in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול picks the offerings he will eat, takes one of the שתי הלחם, and takes four or five of the לחם הפנים.

steps.title: רבי: always five loaves, half for אהרן
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds the כהן גדול always takes five of the לחם הפנים, learning from 'for Aaron and his sons' that he gets half.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: Always five, as it says, 'It shall be for אהרן and for his sons.' This means half for אהרן and half for his sons.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי disagrees with 'four or five' and says the number is always five. He brings a פסוק as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names אהרן separately from his sons. רבי reads this as an equal split: half goes to the כהן גדול and half to all the other כהנים. Only ten of the twelve loaves were actually shared out, so half is five.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול has first choice in offering and in eating. For the לחם הפנים, the ברייתא says four or five, but רבי says always five: half for אהרן and half for his sons.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the special status of the כהן גדול. A single כהן receives as much as all the other כהנים together.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: always five,
as it is said: 'And it shall be for Aaron and for his sons' (Leviticus 24:9) —
half for Aaron
and half for his sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the 'four or five' in Step 7 and offers a fixed number based on a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול always takes five לחם הפנים loaves, half of the distributed loaves, based on 'for אהרן and for his sons.'

steps.title: The ברייתא Seems to Contradict Itself
steps.stepSummary: The first clause of the ברייתא fits רבי, the middle clause fits רבנן, and the last clause is רבי again. Can one ברייתא really switch back and forth like that?
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא is difficult on its own terms. You said the כהן גדול takes one loaf out of the two loaves. Whose view is that? It is רבי, who says he takes half. Now look at the middle clause: four or five of the לחם הפנים. Now we have come to רבנן, who say he does not take half. Now look at the last clause: רבי says he always takes five. So is the first and last clause רבי, and the middle clause רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem inside the ברייתא itself. Its three clauses seem to follow different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One loaf out of two is exactly half, which matches רבי's rule that the כהן גדול gets half. 'Four or five' out of twelve is less than half, which matches רבנן. Then the last clause openly names רבי as the one who disagrees. So it is strange for the first clause to be רבי while the middle clause is רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult: the source contradicts itself.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the problem is about numbers alone. The issue is that the ברייתא appears to follow רבי, then רבנן, then רבי again. A single ברייתא normally keeps to one consistent view.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרַתְּ נוֹטֵל חַלָּה אַחַת מִשְׁתֵּי חַלּוֹת,
phrases.english: you said: he takes one loaf of the two loaves,
whose view is this? It is Rabbi,
who says he takes half.
Say the middle clause:

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע אוֹ חָמֵשׁ מִמַּעֲשֵׂה לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים,
phrases.english: four or five of the shewbread loaves,
now we have come to the Rabbis,
who say: he does not take half.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא סֵיפָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם חָמֵשׁ.
phrases.english: Say the last clause: Rabbi says: always five.
The first and last clauses are Rabbi, and the middle is the Rabbis?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the consistency of the ברייתא quoted in steps 7 and 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the ברייתא about the כהן גדול's portion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking one of two loaves is half, which is רבי's view. Taking four or five of twelve is less than half, which is רבנן's view. The last clause is רבי. So the ברייתא seems to jump between opinions.

steps.title: אביי: Both Early Clauses Follow the Rabbis, Since a Piece Is Undignified
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the first and middle clauses both follow רבנן. With the two loaves, רבנן agree he gets a whole loaf, because giving the כהן גדול a broken piece is not respectful.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the first clause and the middle clause are both רבנן. רבנן agree in the case of a broken piece, because it is not proper to give it to the כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction. He explains that the first clause also follows רבנן, so the ברייתא is consistent after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבנן's math, the כהן גדול should get less than one full loaf of the שתי הלחם. But handing him a broken piece is undignified, so he is given a full loaf instead. That means the first clause is not a proof of רבי. Only the last clause is רבי.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבנן, the כהן גדול normally gets less than half. With the שתי הלחם he still gets a full loaf, out of respect, because a piece is not fitting for him. So the ברייתא is רבנן until רבי's dissent at the end.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of respect for the כהן גדול changes how the division works in practice. It does not change רבנן's basic principle that he gets less than half.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
the first and middle clauses are the Rabbis,
and the Rabbis concede regarding a piece,
that it is not proper conduct
to give it to the High Priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by assigning the first clause to רבנן as well.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the clause: the first clause is shown to fit רבנן because of a practical exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Taking one full loaf out of two must mean taking half, which is רבי's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבנן give a full loaf, because a broken piece is undignified for the כהן גדול. The ברייתא follows רבנן until רבי's dissent in the last clause.
